title: Resolved chain model for the iterated derived evaluation transpose
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Use $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] as the derived category of modules on the one-object site with trivial topology and ring $R$, and $H(X,Y)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Use direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and product Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]. For any $K,L,M\in D(R)$ choose a K-flat complex $P$ representing $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] and K-injective complexes $J,I$ representing $L,M$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Put $A^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(J,I)$ and let $Q$ denote localization from complexes to $D(R)$.
There are canonical isomorphisms in $D(R)$
$$\lambda_P:Q\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_RP)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,\qquad \rho_P:Q\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(P,J),I)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(H(K,L),M).$$
On homogeneous elements $h\in(A^\bullet)^a$, $x\in P^b$, and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(P,J)^c$, the rule
$$E_P(h\otimes x)(f)=(-1)^{bc}h(f(x))$$
defines a chain map $E_P:\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_RP)\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(P,J),I)$ for arbitrary unbounded complexes of this kind. Let $e_{K,L,M}$ be the iterated evaluation transpose of [lem-trf-closed-evaluation-naturality] in the closed symmetric monoidal structure on $D(R)$ given by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] for this one-object site: it transposes the composite that swaps $P$ past the inner Hom and then applies the two evaluation counits. Then
$$\rho_P\circ Q(E_P)=e_{K,L,M}\circ\lambda_P.$$
The isomorphisms and equality use the canonical representative identifications for the chosen representatives, with no boundedness or finite-generation assumptions.

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J)$ and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes P)$. For fixed degrees $a,b,c$, evaluation $h\otimes x\mapsto(f\mapsto(-1)^{bc}h(f(x)))$ is balanced and linear, and lands in $\operatorname{Hom}_R(B^c,I^{a+b+c})$. The product defining the target permits one such component for every $c$. Every element of $T^n$ is a finite sum over $a+b=n$, with each tensor itself a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus these formulas sum to an actual degree-zero graded map $E:T\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(B,I)$; no infinite sum in $I$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0A60 (lemma-evaluate-and-more), finite-support construction before equation beta

proof.text:
For $|h|=a$, $|x|=b$, $|f|=c$, expand the target differential, including its action on $df$:
$$d(E(h\otimes x))(f)=(-1)^{bc}d_Ih(f(x))-(-1)^{a+bc}h(d_Jf(x))+(-1)^{a+bc+c}h(f(d_Px)).$$
Expanding $E(dh\otimes x+(-1)^ah\otimes d_Px)(f)$ gives these same three terms, since $dh=d_Ih-(-1)^ahd_J$ and $(b+1)c=bc+c$. Equality on every product projection and tensor generator proves $dE=Ed$, for all integer degrees, including negative ones.

proof.text: Use the canonical representative comparisons for derived Hom with K-injective target: $QA\simeq H(L,M)$, $QB\simeq H(K,L)$, and $Q\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(B,I)\simeq H(QB,M)$. Their independence of the representatives is the quasi-isomorphism invariance of Hom into K-injectives. The native localization tensorator $\mu_{X,Y}:QX\otimes^L QY\to Q\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes Y)$ is invertible when either factor is K-flat. In particular $\mu_{A,P}^{-1}$, followed by the comparisons $QA\simeq H(L,M)$ and $QP\simeq K$, gives $\lambda_P$. The outer Hom comparison, followed by the contravariant transport of $QB\simeq H(K,L)$, gives $\rho_P$. This uses K-flatness of $P$, not flatness of its individual terms.

source.place: Tag 0A5W (section-RHom), definition by a K-injective target; Tag 0A67 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), chosen representatives

proof.text:
Record explicitly the counit normalization needed below. For any complex $Y$ and K-injective $N$, let $C=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(Y,N)$, $\gamma:QC\simeq H(QY,QN)$, and $v:C\otimes Y\to N$, $g\otimes y\mapsto g(y)$. Then
$$\epsilon_{QY,QN}(\gamma\otimes1)=Q(v)\mu_{C,Y}.$$
Indeed choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Y'\to Y$. Precompose both sides with the isomorphism $1\otimes Qq$. Naturality of $\mu$ and the component identity $v(1\otimes q)=v'\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}(q,N)\otimes1\bigr)$ reduce the equation to the one-K-flat chain-transpose theorem applied to the chain map $C\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(Y',N)$, $g\mapsto gq$. Its transpose is exactly $g\otimes y'\mapsto g(qy')$. The Hom comparison is the canonical one by its quasi-isomorphism invariance, so cancellation of $1\otimes Qq$ proves the displayed equation. This argument does not invert $\mu_{C,Y}$ or require $Y$ to be K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0A5W (section-RHom), tensor-Hom adjunction; Tag 0A67, comparison with the representative evaluations

proof.text:
Let $D=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(B,I)$ and write $v_{Y,N}$ for ordinary evaluation. There is an equality of chain maps
$$v_{B,I}(E\otimes1_B)=v_{J,I}(1_A\otimes v_{P,J})(1_A\otimes\sigma_{P,B}):T\otimes B\to I,$$
with tensor associators inserted. On $h\otimes x\otimes f$ each side is $(-1)^{bc}h(f(x))$: ordinary evaluations introduce no signs, and the single swap introduces $(-1)^{bc}$. These generator equalities establish the whole equation, including all product components.

source.place: Tag 0A61 (remark-sign-explanation), swap of the last two factors followed by two evaluations

proof.text:
Localize the preceding chain equality and precompose with the iterated lax tensorator from $QA\otimes^L QP\otimes^L QB$. Naturality and associativity of this tensorator, and its compatibility with the Koszul braiding, identify the two sides with the corresponding composites in the derived category. Apply the counit equation of step 4 to $(Y,N)=(B,I),(P,J),(J,I)$. Under the comparisons of step 3 the left side becomes the uncurrying of $\rho_P Q(E)\lambda_P^{-1}$; the right side becomes
$$H(L,M)\otimes^L K\otimes^L H(K,L)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\sigma}H(L,M)\otimes^L H(K,L)\otimes^L K\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon}H(L,M)\otimes^L L\xrightarrow{\epsilon}M.$$
The closed-evaluation lemma specifies $e_{K,L,M}$ as the unique transpose of precisely this composite. Injectivity of that adjunction bijection gives $\rho_P Q(E)\lambda_P^{-1}=e_{K,L,M}$, hence the asserted equation. All cancellations are of representative comparison isomorphisms or of $\mu_{A,P}$, whose invertibility was proved in step 3; no other tensorator is inverted.

tool_uses.why: Hom invariance supplies canonical chosen K-injective comparisons; the unit contains no substitute for this generic homological tool.
Canonical lax localization tensorator, one-sided K-flat invertibility, and structural coherence are needed to localize the chain equality.
A flat-term resolution of an arbitrary tensor parameter is used only to check a counit equation.
The generic normalized chain-transpose statement fixes the counit on a flat-term K-flat parameter; it replaces no step of the unit route.
